applies_why: The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to a Luke 2:48-49 father/Father word clash, which is the kind of single-verse/two-sense determination K-S2 governs.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open": I weighed (a) Luke 2:48-49's lower-case father and capital Father are two senses that both stand, so it cannot be UNDERDETERMINED, versus (b) the judge's phrase "immediately qualified" means the single verse is open and hence UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The judge labels the Luke 2:48-49 clash UNDERDETERMINED despite treating it as a father/Father two-sense verse, which K-S2 says is not open.
